stories.headline: ECONOMY UNEXPECTEDLY SHEDS 23,000 JOBS IN JULY, STOCKS RALLY TO A RECORD ON RATE-CUT HOPES
stories.body: Nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 versus a forecast gain of 83,000, and May-June figures were revised down a combined 103,000, even as the unemployment rate held at 4.1% and labor-force participation slid to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years. The S&P 500 rose 0.62% to a record 7,757.64 as traders priced in higher odds of a September Fed rate cut.
stories.explain: A payrolls miss this large shifts the market's estimate of the Fed's reaction function almost instantly, because fed funds futures reprice the odds of a September cut within minutes of the release. Lower expected short-term rates flow through a discounted-cash-flow model as a lower discount rate on future corporate earnings, which mechanically raises today's fair value for equities even though nothing about the earnings themselves has changed. The falling participation rate is the nuance to watch — it suggests some of today's weakness is workers exiting the labor force rather than pure layoffs, a subtly different signal for the Fed than demand destruction.

stories.headline: 2-YEAR YIELD SINKS 5 BPS TO 4.19% AS TRADERS RAMP UP BETS ON A SEPTEMBER FED CUT
stories.body: The policy-sensitive 2-year Treasury yield fell as much as 9 bps intraday to touch 4.15% before settling near 4.19%, its lowest level since July 17, while the 10-year fell a smaller 3 bps to 4.65% — a curve-steepening move typical of a market pricing in near-term easing.
stories.explain: The 2-year yield moves more than the 10-year on a weak jobs report because it's most directly anchored to where the Fed funds rate will sit over the next two years, while the 10-year also embeds long-run growth and inflation expectations that are stickier. When short rates fall faster than long rates, the yield curve steepens — exactly what happened this week — and that steepening is itself a market signal that investors expect the Fed to start cutting rather than merely pause.

stories.headline: S&P 500 CAPS BEST WEEK SINCE APRIL WITH RECORD CLOSE, NASDAQ 100 ADDS ROUGHLY 1%
stories.body: The S&P 500 closed the week at a record 7,757.64 and the Nasdaq 100 gained about 1.2% as tech led the rally on the view that a softer labor market gives the Fed more room to ease. Markets are closed for the weekend; Monday's session will show whether the rally has legs.
stories.explain: 'Bad news is good news' only holds when the market believes the economy is weakening gradually enough that the Fed can offset it with rate cuts before it becomes a genuine growth scare — investors are betting on the soft-landing interpretation of Friday's data rather than a recession signal. That's a real gamble: if next week's CPI print confirms broader deterioration rather than a one-off payrolls miss, the same rate-cut logic that lifted stocks can flip into a growth-scare selloff instead.

stories.headline: GOLD POSTS ITS BEST WEEK SINCE APRIL, UP 7.2%, AS FALLING YIELDS AND A SOFTER DOLLAR PULL IN THE SAME DIRECTION
stories.body: Gold notched roughly a 7.2% weekly advance to about $4,341 an ounce as Treasury yields fell on the jobs miss and the dollar index sank to 99.60, while WTI crude held near $78 with a geopolitical risk premium still priced in around the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.explain: Gold pays no yield, so its opportunity cost falls in lockstep with real interest rates — this week's drop in Treasury yields directly lowered the cost of holding non-yielding bullion instead of interest-bearing bonds, which is the main driver of the rally. A weaker dollar amplifies the move for the same reason it always does: gold is priced in dollars globally, so a softer DXY makes the metal cheaper for foreign buyers and mechanically lifts dollar-denominated demand, layering a currency tailwind on top of the rates story.

stories.headline: SECOND HIDDEN CLIPPERS-KAWHI ENDORSEMENT DEAL SURFACES, LEAVING RAPTORS TRADE IN LIMBO
stories.body: New reporting from Pablo Torre alleges Kawhi Leonard held an undisclosed sponsorship with Daktronics, the company that built the Clippers' Intuit Dome scoreboard, adding to the league's existing probe into his $28M deal with the now-bankrupt Aspiration. The Raptors-Clippers trade that would send Leonard back to Toronto remains on hold until the NBA's salary-cap-circumvention investigation is resolved.

stories.headline: COMMANDERS LT LAREMY TUNSIL TEARS TRICEPS, WILL MISS MOST OF 2026 SEASON
stories.body: Tunsil suffered the injury Saturday fighting off a bull rush from free-agent addition Odafe Oweh in one-on-one drills, just five months after Washington made him the NFL's highest-paid offensive lineman on a two-year, $60.2M extension. Brandon Coleman steps in at left tackle to protect Jayden Daniels as the five-time Pro Bowler undergoes surgery.

stories.headline: ALABAMA'S QB BATTLE TIGHTENS AS RUSSELL OUTDUELS MACK IN FALL CAMP SCRIMMAGE
stories.body: Keelon Russell went 20-of-32 for 229 yards and 4 touchdowns against Austin Mack's 7-of-13, 95 yards and 1 touchdown in Alabama's latest scrimmage, with Kalen DeBoer hoping to name a starter as early as Aug. 17 to replace NFL-bound Ty Simpson.

stories.headline: TENNESSEE JUDGE GRANTS TEXAS TRANSFER A FIFTH SEASON, DEEPENING NCAA'S ELIGIBILITY CRISIS
stories.body: A Tennessee court ruled that Texas transfer Chendall Weaver can play a fifth college season, and he immediately committed to Houston — the latest case forcing administrators toward a blanket eligibility waiver as more players win extra years through litigation ahead of a season that will also see the tournament field grow to 76 teams in 2027.

sports.detail: Fall camp rolled on with a 10 AM practice Sunday under third-year HC Jedd Fisch after Saturday's off day; transfer DL Kai McClendon is nearing a return from injury rehab. Season opener vs. Washington State (Apple Cup) is Sunday, Sept. 6, 4 PM ET on NBC.

Danny Sprinkle is rebuilding via the portal after losing both leading scorers: Hannes Steinbach (18.5 ppg) went 14th overall to Charlotte in the draft, and Zoom Diallo (15.7 ppg) transferred to Kentucky. Wesley Yates III (12.9 ppg) returns as the top scorer off a 16-17 season.

Football Fest packed Lumen Field Saturday for the first fan event there since the Super Bowl parade; second-year DT Rylie Mills kept turning heads in camp and Marshawn Lynch made an appearance. Preseason opener vs. the Cowboys is Saturday, Aug. 15.

Jalen Duren's restricted free agency remains stalled at $35-38M/yr from Detroit against a ~$287M/5-yr ask, with the front office pointing to his playoff dip (10.2 pts/8.5 reb vs. 19.5/10.5 in the regular season) and no rival offer sheet putting pressure on the Pistons. Oct. 1 qualifying-offer deadline looms.

Dropped Sunday's finale 4-1 to Tampa Bay at T-Mobile Park, their second loss to the Rays this weekend. Next: a road series at the Athletics this week as Seattle fights to stay in the thick of a tight AL West race with Houston.

watchlist: CPI report — Wednesday, Aug. 12, 8:30 AM ET — will be the tie-breaker for the Fed's September rate decision after last week's payrolls miss
Alabama QB decision — Kalen DeBoer hopes to name a starter between Russell and Mack as early as Monday, Aug. 17
Seahawks preseason opener vs. Cowboys — Saturday, Aug. 15
Jalen Duren-Pistons contract standoff — Oct. 1 deadline for Duren to accept Detroit's $9.6M qualifying offer
Huskies open the season vs. Washington State (Apple Cup) — Sunday, Sept. 6, Husky Stadium

deepDive.title: Bull Steepening: What This Week's Yield-Curve Move Actually Signals
content: This week's Treasury move was more interesting than the headline jobs number itself: the 2-year yield fell 5 bps to 4.19% while the 10-year fell only 3 bps to 4.65%, steepening the curve. Heading into Wednesday's CPI print, that shape matters as much as the direction, because it tells you which part of the market is doing the repricing — and right now it's overwhelmingly the front end, the part most sensitive to what the Fed does next rather than to long-run growth or inflation expectations.

This is a textbook 'bull steepening': short rates fall faster than long rates, and the whole curve effectively becomes less inverted or more positively sloped. The 2-year is essentially a running average of expected Fed policy over the next two years, so a weak payrolls report gets absorbed there almost instantly as traders mark up the odds of a September cut. The 10-year carries that same policy expectation but blends it with a term premium — compensation investors demand for holding duration risk over a decade — which moves much more slowly and is why it lagged the front end by 2 full percentage points of yield decline this week.

The distinction that gets lost in casual market commentary is bull steepening versus bear steepening. In 2022's bear steepening, long yields rose on inflation and fiscal-deficit fears even as the Fed hiked — a bad, discount-rate-driven move for stocks. What happened this week is the opposite and more benign: front-end yields falling because growth is cooling faster than expected, historically the same pattern seen in mid-2019 just before the Fed's three insurance cuts, when the curve steepened for months heading into an easing cycle rather than a recession.

The reason this matters for Monday's open and beyond is that Wednesday's CPI print is the next data point that can confirm or break this narrative. If inflation cooperates, the bull-steepening trade likely continues — good for equities via lower discount rates, good for gold via lower real yields, exactly what powered this week's rally. But if CPI surprises hot, the Fed's room to cut narrows fast, the front end could snap back up, and the same curve move that just fueled a record S&P close could reverse into the kind of growth-scare repricing that catches a record-chasing market offside.
